newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends weaker in lackluster trade.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends weaker in lackluster trade.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended weaker in uneventful dealings on Thursday, in what traders said was mainly a local-dominated market.
Turnover on the day was unimpressive, they said, with only an estimated 4,613 lots changing hands.
"There's no news, no weather and no interest," said one trader. "There's nothing to say about this market."

Benchmark September contract fell 1.05 cents a lb on the day, to 160.45 cents, after ranging between 163.50 and 159.00 cents. Spot July, which expires on Monday, ended 0.35 cents weaker, at 186.90 cents, while the outer months closed down 0.25 to 1.45 cents.
The July/September switch widened to 26.45 cents compared with 25.75 cents at the close on Wednesday, while the September/December switch narrowed to 12.85 cents from 13.20 cents.

New York coffee prices headed higher at the opening bell, on local and light commission house buying, traders said. But September's inability to breach resistance at 165.00 cents per lb prompted locals to turn around and unload positions.
Continued frost-free conditions in leading-producer Brazil and a build in coffee stocks certified for delivery against the exchange weighed on sentiment, traders said.
CSCE reported after Thursday's close that certified coffee inventories rose by 1,737 60-kg bags as of July 16, to 77,151 bags. An additional 36,587 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
Technically, traders said September still faced support at 155.00 cents, with the next level seen at 150.00 cents. Resistance was seen near 165.00 cents.

On the fundamental side, U.K. trade house E D & F Man said in its June/July coffee report that world consumer coffee stocks rose in May to 10.9 million bags, compared with 9.9 million in April and 9.1 million bags in May 1996.
Man said U.S. stocks rose to 1.97 million bags in May from 1.85 million in April, but were 294,000 lower than in May 1996.
Earlier this week, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported that consumer coffee stocks stowed in U.S. warehouses rose in June by 139,000 60-kg bags, to 2,116,000 bags.
